messages:
Anya (People Ops): Heads up — Sylvia's birthday is next Friday (Apr 2). Thinking through a couple low-effort options for the team present: tiny desk parade in-office (2-min sing + confetti poppers) or handwritten card + remote GIF chain for folks who are remote. Also open to a small pastry box. Thoughts? :birthday:
Jonas: Love the parade idea if she's in office. Feels fun and quick.
Priya: Sylvia's planning to be in SF that day but arriving after lunch. Parade could still work. Anyone know if she has any allergies?
Tanya: Handwritten card + digital chain feels more inclusive to remote folks. We could also do a small pastry box for the office people.
Anya (People Ops): Good call on inclusivity. How about formalizing options so we can vote: A) Tiny desk parade + pastry box for on-site folks B) Handwritten card + e-card + $25 bakery credit mailed C) Mini care package (succulent + snacks) mailed. React with :one:, :two:, or :three:.
Jonas: :one:
Priya: :two: (B sounds best to me)
Tanya: :three: but also fine with B — leaning towards something we can send to everyone.
Micah: If we go with mailing, can we collect addresses via a short Google form? I can compile and print signatures for the card.
Anya (People Ops): Yes — I'll make a form after this. Also noting any scent/balloon allergies before we commit. @Sylvia — low-key surprise okay or would you rather we don't do surprises? No pressure either way.
Sylvia: Aww you all <3 — low-key surprise is fine! Please avoid balloons (scent/asthma). Pastries and cards are perfect. :)
Anya (People Ops): Noted — no balloons. Consensus looks like B (cards + e-card + bakery credit). I'll post the address/form and deadline (please submit by Tue 4/30). Thanks everyone! :tada:
celebrations-bot: Reminder set — collect addresses via the form in #people-ops by Tue 4/30. :white_check_mark:
